title: Formal writing and registers
objectives: I can plan and write a structured essay with an introduction, development and conclusion, choosing each connector for the logical relation it expresses.
I can write formal letters and cover letters with the correct address, request formulas and closing, and replace spoken forms with their written equivalents.
I can turn a spoken clause into a concise noun phrase by nominalization and explain how the suffix fixes the noun's gender and spelling.
I can explain why formal words are spelled and stressed as they are, and decide crase, hyphens and commas by applying a test instead of guessing.

vocabulary.note: Opens the first argument of a list; continue with em segundo lugar and por fim. Lugar is lu-GAR, stressed on the last syllable because the ending r predicts it, so it needs no accent. Primeiro contains the diphthong ei, as in English day.

example.target: Em primeiro lugar, é preciso definir o problema.
example.source: First of all, the problem must be defined.
example.source_literal: In first place, is necessary to-define the problem.

vocabulary.note: Formal addition; the spoken equivalent is além disso. It is three words fused: a + de + mais. Ai is a diphthong and the ending is predicts stress on the last syllable, so it is a-de-MAIS with no accent.

example.target: Ademais, o custo da obra aumentou.
example.source: Moreover, the cost of the construction work increased.

vocabulary.note: Formal; marks a result that follows logically from the previous sentence. The spoken equivalents are então and por isso. In conseguinte the u of gui is silent and the g is hard: con-se-GUIN-te, with a nasal i because the n ends its syllable.

example.target: A verba acabou; por conseguinte, o projeto parou.
example.source: The funds ran out; consequently, the project stopped.

vocabulary.note: Introduces the summary or conclusion. Similar: em síntese, em resumo. Síntese is stressed on the third to last syllable (SÍN-te-se), so it always carries an accent.

example.target: Em suma, a educação transforma a sociedade.
example.source: In short, education transforms society.

vocabulary.note: A cognate of thesis: English th is written t (a tese, o teatro, a teoria). The single s between vowels is [z], so the word is TE-zi. The stressed e is open, which the spelling does not show.

example.target: A tese do texto é que o acesso à leitura é desigual.
example.source: The thesis of the text is that access to reading is unequal.

vocabulary.note: Nouns in -mento are masculine. Stress is on men (ar-gu-MEN-to), the second to last syllable, as the ending o predicts. The u of gu is pronounced because it is followed by m, not by e or i.

example.target: Cada parágrafo deve apresentar um argumento claro.
example.source: Each paragraph should present a clear argument.

vocabulary.note: From redigir, to draft. Not the English redaction, which means editing out. It also means the editorial office of a newspaper. The ENEM is the national university entrance exam, and its written part is called a redação. Re-da-ÇÃO: ç is [s] before a, and the tilde of ão already marks the stress.

example.target: A redação do exame vale mil pontos.
example.source: The essay in the exam is worth a thousand points.

vocabulary.note: Required at the end of ENEM essays. It names an agent, an action, a means, a purpose and a detail. Intervenção ends in -ção like redação, so it is feminine.

example.target: A proposta de intervenção deve ser detalhada e viável.
example.source: The intervention proposal must be detailed and feasible.

vocabulary.note: Short for curriculum vitae, Latin for course of life. It is also the word for a school curriculum, so context decides. Stressed on the third to last syllable (cur-RÍ-cu-lo), which no ending predicts, so it is always accented. The rr is one strong r sound.

example.target: Encaminhei meu currículo para a empresa.
example.source: I sent my résumé to the company.

vocabulary.note: Apresentar means to present or to introduce. The ending -ção makes the noun feminine and is said [sɐ̃w̃] with the stress on the last syllable.

example.target: A carta de apresentação deve ser curta e objetiva.
example.source: The cover letter should be short and to the point.

vocabulary.note: From relatar, to relate or report. The final io counts as two syllables in the stress rule, so re-la-TÓ-ri-o is stressed on the third to last and must carry an accent. The o is open, so the acute.

example.target: O relatório mensal será entregue na sexta.
example.source: The monthly report will be delivered on Friday.

vocabulary.note: Used when a document travels with the message. Anexo is also the noun annex. The x between vowels is [ks] here (a-NE-ksu); the spelling does not predict it, so learn it with the word.

example.target: Envio, em anexo, os documentos solicitados.
example.source: I am sending the requested documents, attached.
example.source_literal: I-send, in annex, the documents requested.

vocabulary.note: Followed by an infinitive when the subject does not change. With que (a fim de que) it takes the subjunctive, because the aim has not yet happened. Fim ends in im, a nasal vowel: the lips do not close.

example.target: Reunimos a equipe a fim de definir as prioridades.
example.source: We gathered the team in order to define the priorities.

vocabulary.note: Introduces a source or an agreement: conforme combinado (as agreed), conforme o relatório (according to the report). Segue is a fixed letter formula, literally follows. The on before f is a nasal vowel.

example.target: Conforme combinado, segue o contrato.
example.source: As agreed, the contract is attached.

vocabulary.note: Physically in front of; figuratively faced with. The d before i is [dʒ] and the an is nasal: dji-AN-tchi.

example.target: Diante dos fatos, a diretoria decidiu agir.
example.source: In view of the facts, the board decided to act.
example.source_literal: In-front of-the facts, the board decided to-act.

vocabulary.note: Written as one word, from sobre (over) and tudo (everything). Stress is on tu (so-bre-TU-do), the second to last syllable, as the ending o predicts.

example.target: O país precisa, sobretudo, de investimento em educação.
example.source: The country needs, above all, investment in education.
example.source_literal: The country needs, over-all, of investment in education.

vocabulary.note: Cabe is from caber, to fit: what fits the situation is what is appropriate to say. Variants: cabe destacar, cabe salientar. In ressaltar the ss is one [s] and the l that ends a syllable is [w]: res-saw-TAR.

example.target: Cabe ressaltar que os dados ainda são preliminares.
example.source: It is worth emphasizing that the data are still preliminary.
example.source_literal: It-fits to-emphasize that the data still are preliminary.

vocabulary.note: A formal verb for evidence that supports a claim. The rr is one strong r, and the final r makes the last syllable the stressed one: cor-ro-bo-RAR.

example.target: Os números corroboram a hipótese do autor.
example.source: The numbers corroborate the author's hypothesis.

vocabulary.note: A nominalization of conscientizar, to make conscious. The sc before i is one [s], the ti is said tchi, the z stands between vowels, and -ção makes the noun feminine.

example.target: A conscientização da população é essencial.
example.source: Raising public awareness is essential.

vocabulary.note: The most common closing in Brazilian business letters and emails. Cordialmente is slightly warmer. It is the feminine adjective atenciosa plus the adverb ending -mente, stressed on men. The s between vowels is [z].

example.target: Atenciosamente, Camila Duarte.
example.source: Sincerely, Camila Duarte.

dialogues.title: Aula de redação
dialogues.context: Teacher Lúcia reviews the structure of an essay for the ENEM, the national university entrance exam, with two students.

lines.speaker: Lúcia
lines.target: Turma, hoje vamos revisar a estrutura da redação do ENEM. Quem lembra quantos parágrafos ela costuma ter?
lines.source: Class, today we will review the structure of the ENEM essay. Who remembers how many paragraphs it usually has?
lines.source_literal: Class, today we-go to-review the structure of-the essay of-the ENEM. Who remembers how-many paragraphs it is-accustomed to-have?

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.target: Quatro, professora: uma introdução, dois parágrafos de desenvolvimento e uma conclusão.
lines.source: Four, teacher: an introduction, two development paragraphs and a conclusion.

lines.speaker: Lúcia
lines.target: Exato. Na introdução, apresentamos o tema e defendemos uma tese. Qual é o erro mais comum nessa parte?
lines.source: Exactly. In the introduction we present the topic and defend a thesis. What is the most common mistake in this part?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.target: Acho que é fugir do tema ou escrever de forma muito vaga, sem posicionamento.
lines.source: I think it is drifting off the topic or writing in a very vague way, without taking a position.
lines.source_literal: I-find that it-is to-flee from-the theme or to-write in form very vague, without positioning.

lines.speaker: Lúcia
lines.target: Isso. No desenvolvimento, cada parágrafo precisa de um argumento e de um exemplo que o sustente.
lines.source: Right. In the development, each paragraph needs an argument and an example that supports it.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.target: Posso usar conectivos como ademais e por conseguinte para ligar as ideias?
lines.source: Can I use connectors such as ademais and por conseguinte to link the ideas?

lines.speaker: Lúcia
lines.target: Pode, mas sem exagerar. Conectivos demais deixam o texto artificial. Use só quando fizerem sentido.
lines.source: You can, but don't overdo it. Too many connectors make the text artificial. Use them only when they make sense.
lines.source_literal: Can, but without exaggerating. Connectors too-many leave the text artificial. Use only when they-make sense.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.target: E na conclusão a gente precisa fazer uma proposta de intervenção, né?
lines.source: And in the conclusion we need to make an intervention proposal, right?
lines.source_literal: And in-the conclusion the people needs to-make a proposal of intervention, isn't-it?

lines.speaker: Lúcia
lines.target: Sim, e ela deve ter agente, ação, meio, finalidade e detalhamento. Sem isso, você perde pontos.
lines.source: Yes, and it must have an agent, an action, a means, a purpose and a detail. Without that, you lose points.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.target: Entendi. Vou treinar com um tema por semana e mandar para a senhora corrigir.
lines.source: Understood. I will practice with one topic a week and send it to you to correct.
lines.source_literal: I-understood. I-go to-train with one topic per week and send to the lady to-correct.

lines.speaker: Lúcia
lines.target: Combinado. Lembrem-se: linguagem formal, sem gírias e sem abreviações de internet.
lines.source: Agreed. Remember: formal language, no slang and no internet abbreviations.
lines.source_literal: Combined. Remember-yourselves: language formal, without slang and without abbreviations of internet.

dialogues.title: Carta de apresentação
dialogues.context: Renata is applying to a multinational company. Her mentor Carlos reviews her cover letter and corrects the tone.

lines.speaker: Renata
lines.target: Carlos, você pode olhar minha carta de apresentação? Estou me candidatando a uma vaga numa multinacional.
lines.source: Carlos, can you look at my cover letter? I am applying for a position at a multinational.
lines.source_literal: Carlos, you can look-at my letter of presentation? I-am myself applying to a vacancy in-a multinational.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.target: Claro. Você começou com oi, pessoal? Melhor evitar. Use prezados senhores, ou o nome do responsável, se souber.
lines.source: Sure. Did you start with oi, pessoal? Better to avoid that. Use prezados senhores, or the name of the person in charge, if you know it.
lines.source_literal: Of-course. You started with hi, people? Better to-avoid. Use dear sirs, or the name of-the responsible-person, if you-know.

lines.speaker: Renata
lines.target: Escrevi oi, tudo bem? Vou trocar. E para o pedido, posso dizer quero muito trabalhar aí?
lines.source: I wrote oi, tudo bem? I will change it. And for the request, can I say quero muito trabalhar aí?
lines.source_literal: I-wrote hi, all well? I-go to-swap. And for the request, can-I say I-want much to-work there?

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.target: Prefira algo como venho por meio desta manifestar meu interesse pela vaga. É mais adequado ao contexto.
lines.source: Prefer something like venho por meio desta manifestar meu interesse pela vaga. It suits the context better.
lines.source_literal: Prefer something like I-come by means of-this to-express my interest by-the vacancy. It-is more suitable to-the context.

lines.speaker: Renata
lines.target: E aqui eu escrevi pra. Pode?
lines.source: And here I wrote pra. Is that okay?
lines.source_literal: And here I wrote pra. Can-it?

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.target: Não. Escreva para. Em texto formal, evite pra, tá e a gente. Prefira nós ou a primeira pessoa do singular.
lines.source: No. Write para. In formal text, avoid pra, tá and a gente. Prefer nós or the first person singular.

lines.speaker: Renata
lines.target: E na despedida? Beijos está fora, né?
lines.source: And for the sign-off? Beijos is out, right?
lines.source_literal: And in-the farewell? Kisses is outside, isn't-it?

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.target: Com certeza. Use atenciosamente ou cordialmente, seguido do seu nome completo.
lines.source: Definitely. Use atenciosamente or cordialmente, followed by your full name.
lines.source_literal: With certainty. Use attentively or cordially, followed by-the your name complete.

lines.speaker: Renata
lines.target: Também vou anexar o currículo e mencionar isso no texto.
lines.source: I will also attach the résumé and mention it in the text.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.target: Boa ideia. Escreva: encaminho, em anexo, meu currículo. Depois a gente revisa a pontuação.
lines.source: Good idea. Write: encaminho, em anexo, meu currículo. Then we will review the punctuation.
lines.source_literal: Good idea. Write: I-send-on, in annex, my résumé. Afterwards the people reviews the punctuation.

dialogues.title: Revisão ortográfica
dialogues.context: Fernanda, an editor, reviews the report of Paulo, an intern, together with her colleague Sônia, and points out spellings from before the 2009 Orthographic Agreement.

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.target: Paulo, revisei seu relatório. Está bom, mas há alguns problemas de ortografia.
lines.source: Paulo, I reviewed your report. It is good, but there are some spelling problems.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.target: Pode mostrar? Achei que tinha conferido tudo.
lines.source: Can you show me? I thought I had checked everything.

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.target: Você escreveu anti-social com hífen. Depois do Acordo Ortográfico, o correto é antissocial, com dois s e sem hífen.
lines.source: You wrote anti-social with a hyphen. After the Orthographic Agreement, the correct form is antissocial, with two s and no hyphen.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.target: Verdade, lembrei agora. E com os prefixos auto e infra também?
lines.source: True, I remember now. And with the prefixes auto and infra too?

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.target: Sim: autoestima, infraestrutura. Mas usamos hífen antes de h, como em anti-higiênico.
lines.source: Yes: autoestima, infraestrutura. But we use a hyphen before h, as in anti-higiênico.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.target: E a palavra lingüiça? Escrevi com trema.
lines.source: And the word lingüiça? I wrote it with a diaeresis.

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.target: O trema não existe mais em português, só em nomes estrangeiros, como Müller. Hoje se escreve linguiça e frequência.
lines.source: The diaeresis no longer exists in Portuguese, only in foreign names such as Müller. Today we write linguiça and frequência.
lines.source_literal: The trema not exists more in Portuguese, only in names foreign, like Müller. Today itself-writes linguiça and frequência.

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.target: Outro ponto: você escreveu vou a reunião. Como é a preposição a mais o artigo a, precisa de crase: vou à reunião.
lines.source: Another point: you wrote vou a reunião. Since it is the preposition a plus the article a, it needs crase: vou à reunião.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.target: Ah, sempre erro a crase. Vou fazer uma lista de regras.
lines.source: Oh, I always get the crase wrong. I will make a list of rules.
lines.source_literal: Ah, always I-err the crase. I-go to-make a list of rules.

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.target: Boa ideia. E lembre que ideia e heroico perderam o acento agudo.
lines.source: Good idea. And remember that ideia and heroico lost their acute accent.

grammar.title: Spelling and sound: the words of formal writing
grammar.explanation:
Formal vocabulary looks harder than everyday vocabulary, but it is not irregular. The rules of the first lessons apply unchanged: the letters and the sounds they stand for, the default stress rule with its accent marks, and the nasal vowels. What is new is the kind of word. Formal Portuguese is full of long words built from Latin and Greek parts, and such words fall into a few families whose spelling and stress follow fixed patterns. Learn the patterns and a word you have never seen can be read, stressed and spelled. English speakers have a real advantage here, because English borrowed the same Latin parts, so most of these words are cognates, meaning words related to an English word through a shared origin.

Four correspondences do most of the work. English -tion and -sion correspond to Portuguese -ção and -são (education, educação; decision, decisão). English -ity corresponds to -dade (inequality, desigualdade). English -ence and -ance correspond to -ência and -ância (importance, importância; violence, violência). English -ly corresponds to -mente (sincerely, sinceramente). The Portuguese endings carry grammatical gender, which fixes the article: a redação, a conscientização, a desigualdade and a importância are feminine, while nouns in -mento are masculine (o argumento, o investimento). The languages differ in stress. English stress moves around with the suffix (PHO-to-graph, pho-TOG-ra-phy) and is never written. Portuguese stress is predicted by the last letters of the word and is marked only when it breaks that prediction.

The ending -ção. The cedilla writes the sound [s] before a, because a plain c would be [k] there. The letters ão are the nasal diphthong, said like the ow of English now through the nose, and the default rule gives the ending ão stress on the last syllable. So redação is re-da-ÇÃO: the tilde marks the nasal sound and, because no other accent is present, the stress as well, and nothing more is needed. The plural is -ções (redações), with the nasal diphthong õe. The related ending -são, after a vowel, sounds different, [z], because a single s between two vowel sounds is [z]: decisão is de-ci-ZÃO, with the z of English zoo. The ending -ssão is [s], exactly like -ção (discussão). So in these endings the sound tells you the spelling: [s] is written ç or ss, and [z] between vowels is written s. Whether a given word uses ç or ss must be learned with the word, since they sound the same. After a consonant, -são is [s] (pensão, versão), because the s is no longer between vowels.

Final -ia and -io. Spelling counts a final ia, io, ua or uo as two syllables, even though speech often runs them into one beat. That decides the accent. Relatório is re-la-TÓ-ri-o: counted that way, the stress is on the third to last syllable, which no ending predicts, so an accent is always written, and the open ó takes the acute. The same reasoning gives importância, violência, Excelência, médio and gíria. Before m or n, a stressed a, e or o is written with the circumflex (â, ê, ô) by the convention from the lesson on accent marks, which is why importância and Excelência carry a circumflex and relatório an acute. Compare Senhoria: the stress is on the i itself (se-nho-RI-a), so the word is stressed on the second to last syllable and, like tia, needs no accent.

Adverbs in -mente. An adverb is a word that says how, when or to what degree something happens. Portuguese forms many of them by adding -mente to the feminine form of an adjective: atencioso, atenciosa, atenciosamente; consequente, consequentemente. Adjectives with a single form for both genders do not change: cordial, cordialmente. The ending comes from a Latin word meaning mind, used in phrases such as with an attentive mind, which is why it is a whole stressed syllable and not a small suffix. The default rule gives the final e stress on the second to last syllable, so the main stress falls on men: a-ten-ci-o-sa-MEN-te. The base word loses its written accent when -mente is added, because the base keeps only a weaker secondary stress: fácil gives facilmente and rápida gives rapidamente. The sounds follow the usual rules: the s between vowels in atenciosa is [z], ci is [si], and the t before the final e is [tʃ], like the ch of English cheese.

Silent and pronounced u. In que, qui, gue and gui the u is normally silent and the q or g keeps its hard sound: conseguinte is con-se-GUIN-te with a hard g, and the in is a nasal i because the n ends its syllable. Adquirir, to acquire, has the same silent u (qui is [ki]). In a few words the u is pronounced, as in consequentemente, frequência, linguiça and tranquilo. The two dots once written over the u (lingüiça) marked these words; since 2009 nothing marks them, so you learn which words they are. Before a and o the u is always pronounced: quaisquer is quais-QUER, with the sound [kw], and it is stressed on the last syllable because it ends in r.

The other letters follow the sounds lesson. The r at the start of ressaltar is the strong r, and the rr of corroborar and currículo is also one strong r. The nh of senhor is [ɲ], like the ny of canyon. The ss of impasse and ressaltar is one [s], the sound a single s could not give between vowels. The x of anexo is [ks], and the xc of Excelência is a plain [s]. An l that ends a syllable is [w], so ressaltar sounds like res-saw-TAR. A d before i is [dʒ], like the j of jeans, as in diante. An m or n that ends a syllable only nasalizes the vowel before it: fim, conforme, impasse, importância. Finally, the spelling cannot say whether an unmarked stressed e or o is open or closed: the stressed e of tese is open, and nothing in the spelling shows it. That is learned with the word.

To read any formal word, run the steps from the sounds lesson: look for marks, group the letters that work as a unit, resolve c, g, s, x, r, l, t and d by their neighbours, weaken the final vowels, then find the stress. The table applies the procedure to the words of this unit.

examples.source: The report shows the importance of research.

examples.target: Consequentemente, a frequência das aulas melhorou.
examples.source: Consequently, class attendance improved.

examples.target: A aprendizagem exige dedicação.
examples.source: Learning requires dedication.

grammar.title: Essay structure and cohesive connectors
grammar.explanation:
A formal argument is built so that the reader always knows where they are and why the next sentence follows. The standard school and exam text in Brazil is the dissertação, an argumentative essay (from dissertar, to set out a subject in writing). It has three parts. The introdução presents the theme and states a tese, the single claim the text will defend. The desenvolvimento usually has two paragraphs, and each gives one argumento supported by an example, a fact, a figure or a quotation. The conclusão restates the thesis and, in exams such as the ENEM, adds a proposta de intervenção that names who should act (agente), what they should do (ação), how (meio), why (finalidade) and with what further detail (detalhamento). English school essays follow the same plan; what differs is that a Brazilian exam grades the explicit presence of each element.

A connector (conectivo) is a word or phrase that states how one idea relates to the one before it. Choose it by the relation, not by taste. The relations are addition (another point of the same kind), contrast (a point that pulls the other way), cause (the reason), consequence (the result), concession and conclusion. Concession means granting a point that seems to weaken your claim before showing that it does not: Although there is progress, the challenges remain. Cause and consequence are mirror images: visto que gives the reason first, por conseguinte gives the result after it. English has the same relations (moreover, however, since, therefore, although, in short); Portuguese simply has more formal options for each, and many are transparent compounds, as the second column of the table shows.

The connector also decides the mood of the verb that follows it, which you met in the subjunctive lessons. The indicative is used when the writer asserts something as a fact; the subjunctive when the clause is granted, aimed at or not yet real. Visto que, uma vez que and já que present a cause as an established fact, so they take the indicative. Embora and ainda que take the subjunctive: the fact may well be true, but the writer concedes it without resting the argument on it. A fim de que, which states a purpose that has not yet been achieved, takes the subjunctive too. With a fim de plus an infinitive, the subject of both verbs is normally the same.

Position and punctuation follow from the relation. Contudo, entretanto, todavia, no entanto, porém, portanto and por conseguinte can start a sentence or sit inside it between commas: O problema, contudo, persiste. Mas is different: it cannot move, and it stands at the start of its clause after a comma. A connector that opens a sentence is followed by a comma. When it joins two complete clauses in one sentence, a semicolon stands before it: A verba acabou; por conseguinte, o projeto parou. Finally, vary and ration the connectors. One per logical step is enough; a text that opens every sentence with one sounds mechanical, which is what the teacher means by conectivos demais in the first dialogue.

examples.target: Em primeiro lugar, o acesso à educação ainda é desigual.
examples.source: First of all, access to education is still unequal.
examples.source_literal: In first place, the access to-the education still is unequal.

examples.target: Visto que o investimento é baixo, o problema persiste.
examples.source: Since investment is low, the problem persists.
examples.source_literal: Seen that the investment is low, the problem persists.

examples.target: Embora haja avanços, os desafios continuam grandes.
examples.source: Although there is progress, the challenges remain great.

grammar.title: Register: formal address, request formulas and closings
grammar.explanation:
A register is the level of formality of language, chosen by your relationship to the reader and the setting. Portuguese shows register in more places than English: in the word for you, in the form of the verb, in vocabulary and in fixed phrases. One principle runs through all of them: formal writing creates distance by addressing the reader as a title instead of as you. A title is a noun, so it takes a third person verb, as in English Your Honor is mistaken. That is why o senhor, a senhora, Vossa Senhoria and Vossa Excelência all take the same verb forms as ele and ela.

The opening. Prezado is the past participle of prezar, to value, so Prezado Senhor is literally Valued Sir, and like any adjective it agrees with the person: Prezada Senhora, Prezados Senhores. Senhor comes from a Latin word meaning older, which is why it carries respect. Ilustríssimo is ilustre (illustrious) with the superlative ending -íssimo, so Ilustríssimo Senhor is literally Most Illustrious Sir, used in very formal addresses. Vossa Senhoria (Your Lordship) and Vossa Excelência (Your Excellency) are treatment pronouns: the first for officials and company heads, the second for the highest offices such as presidents, ministers, legislators and judges. The noun is feminine and the verb is third person singular, but an adjective agrees with the actual person: Vossa Excelência está convencida, said of a woman.

The closing. Atenciosamente (attentively) is the standard formula; Cordialmente is slightly warmer; Respeitosamente is the most deferential; Cordiais saudações means cordial greetings. The closing is followed by your full name. Beijos, abraços and valeu belong to friends.

Spoken forms to replace. Fast speech shortens words, and writing has no tone of voice to compensate, so the written register keeps the full form: para, not pra; está, not tá; nós, not a gente; você or o senhor, not cê. Do not confuse these with num and numa, which are the standard contractions of em + um and em + uma and are not errors in writing. Fillers such as né and tipo and farewells such as valeu are left out. The change often comes in bundles: A gente vai analisar becomes Analisaremos, which changes the pronoun, the tense (the simple future) and the ending at once. Vocabulary shifts the same way: solicitar for pedir, informar for avisar, adquirir for comprar, realizar for fazer. English has the same two layers (ask and request, buy and acquire); in Portuguese both layers are Latin in origin, and the difference is between the everyday word and the learned one.

Requests are softened, not shortened. English adds please and would. Formal Portuguese writing uses four devices. First, a verb of request plus que plus the present subjunctive: Solicito que me envie o relatório, where the subjunctive presents the action as wanted but not yet real. Second, the conditional: Gostaria de solicitar. Third, the opening Venho por meio desta followed by an infinitive, literally I come by means of this, where this is the letter itself and desta is de + esta. Fourth, fixed phrases such as Encaminho em anexo and Coloco-me à disposição. Avoid a bare command (Envie o relatório) in a first contact.

Pronoun placement follows the written rules of the lesson on advanced pronouns. A verb that begins its clause takes the pronoun after it with a hyphen (Coloco-me à disposição), while que pulls the pronoun before the verb (Solicito que me envie). Note also the crase in à disposição, the fusion of a and a, explained in its own note below. Official documents use the third person or the impersonal; a cover letter uses the first person singular (Venho, Encaminho); an institution speaking as a body uses the first person plural (Informamos que).

grammar.title: Nominalization and concise noun phrases
grammar.explanation:
Three terms first. A noun names a thing or an idea; a verb names an action or a state; a clause is a unit that has its own verb and subject. Speech builds meaning by chaining clauses with conjunctions: Como o preço aumentou, as famílias compraram menos. Formal writing often packs a whole clause into a noun phrase by turning its verb into a noun. This is called nominalization (nominalização). English does it too in formal style (The increase in price reduced consumption, instead of Because the price increased, people bought less), but formal Portuguese does it far more, and it is one of the clearest marks of a written register.

How it works. The noun names the action, and the former subject moves after de: o preço aumentou becomes o aumento do preço (de + o). The former object also follows de: conscientizar a população becomes a conscientização da população. The preposition which replaces the conjunction carries the logical relation: porque becomes devido a, em virtude de or por causa de; quando becomes com or na; se becomes mediante; para que becomes com vistas a. Word for word, devido a is owed to (devido is the participle of dever, to owe), em virtude de is in virtue of, mediante is through, por meio de is by means of, and diante de is in front of. Since these prepositions meet an article, contractions and crase follow: devido ao aumento, em virtude da chuva, devido à chuva.

Forming the noun. The ending decides both the spelling and the gender, so the article comes for free. The endings -ção and -são (educação, decisão), -dade (desigualdade), -ência and -ância (importância, violência) and -agem (aprendizagem) are feminine; -mento (investimento, crescimento) is masculine. Some nouns have no special suffix: aumentar gives o aumento, in which the ending -ar is replaced by o and the noun is masculine, and chegar gives a chegada, with the feminine ending -ada. Ler gives a leitura, with -ura. The suffix also fixes the sound: -ção is [s], decisão has [z] between vowels, and the sc of crescimento is one [s]. English can use an -ing form as a noun (the rising of prices); Portuguese cannot use its -ndo form (the gerund) as a noun, so o preço aumentando is not a possible replacement for porque o preço aumentou.

Limits. A nominalized phrase has no tense or mood of its own; the main verb carries them. Mediante a conscientização da população, o problema tende a diminuir can only be read as future or general because of tende. Nominalization also hides who acted: devido ao aumento does not say who raised the price. In formal writing that impersonality is often welcome, but it can hide a vagueness that a clause would expose. Two or three noun phrases per sentence are enough; beyond that the sentence becomes heavy and the reader loses the thread.

grammar.title: Crase: when the preposition a meets the article a
grammar.explanation:
The grave accent on à has one job: it records that the preposition a has fused with an a that follows it, most often the feminine article a (the demonstratives aquele, aquela and aquilo, covered below, are the other case). Crase is Greek for blending. A preposition is a small word that links a verb or noun to its complement (a means to or at); an article is the small word before a noun (a means the, as means the in the plural). You cannot hear the accent, because à is a plain a a little longer, so crase is a matter of writing, and it must be decided by asking two questions. First, does the word before require the preposition a? Second, does the word after take the article a or as? Only when both answers are yes do you write à or às. English has no equivalent, because English does not fuse prepositions and articles, but you already know the Portuguese habit from do, no and pelo.

The first question. Many verbs are followed by a: ir a, chegar a, referir-se a, assistir a, responder a, agradar a. Some adjectives and nouns are too (fiel a, acesso a). Clock times carry the preposition a as well: Chegaremos às dez horas, à uma hora, à meia-noite. Fixed phrases built on feminine nouns carry the fused form even when no verb demands it, because the article is part of the phrase: à noite, à tarde, à direita, à esquerda, à vista, à disposição, às vezes.

The second question. The word after must be feminine and must take a definite article (a, as). The test is to swap in a masculine noun: if you would write ao, the feminine version takes à. Vou ao banco, so Vou à reunião. A second test uses the verb voltar (to return): if you can say volto da (from the), the place takes an article and needs crase; if you say volto de, it does not. Volto da Bahia, so Chegamos à Bahia; volto de Curitiba, so Chegamos a Curitiba.

When there is no crase. Before masculine words (a pé, a cavalo, ao banco), before verbs (a partir de amanhã), before pronouns that take no article (a ela, a você, a esta), before the indefinite article (a uma reunião, since uma is not the article a), before a plural noun used without any article (Refiro-me a questões técnicas, but Refiro-me às questões técnicas when the questions are specific), and between repeated words (cara a cara, passo a passo). Before a feminine singular possessive (minha, sua, nossa), crase is optional, because the article is optional there: à sua disposição and a sua disposição are both correct. The demonstratives aquele, aquela and aquilo start with the letter a, which fuses with the preposition: a + aquele = àquele, a + aquilo = àquilo.

Why it matters. Crase changes meaning. Compare Refiro-me à reunião (a specific meeting, with the article) and Refiro-me a reuniões (meetings in general, without one). In formal writing, crase is checked as carefully as agreement, because the errors are common and visible.

grammar.title: Spelling after the 2009 Orthographic Agreement: hyphens, accents and the trema
grammar.explanation:
The Orthographic Agreement is a treaty of the Portuguese-speaking countries, signed in 1990, which unified spelling rules. It came into force in Brazil in 2009 and has been mandatory since 2016. Older books and some writers still use the earlier spellings, which is why a reviewer in the dialogue corrects them. The changes follow the logic of the reading rules, so they can be understood and not only memorized.

The trema. The two dots over the u (lingüiça, freqüência, tranqüilo) once showed that the u of gue, gui, que and qui is pronounced. They were abolished for Portuguese words, and the pronunciation did not change: linguiça, frequência and tranquilo are still said with the u. You learn which words those are. Foreign names keep their original spelling, so Müller keeps its dots; they are German and not Portuguese.

Accents removed. The acute was dropped from the open diphthongs ei and oi in words stressed on the second to last syllable: ideia, heroico, jiboia, assembleia, geleia. It stays where the diphthong is stressed on the last syllable, where the accent is still needed: papéis, herói, céu, dói. The circumflex was dropped from the first vowel of a doubled pair: voo, enjoo, abençoo, and the verb forms leem, veem, creem and deem. Compare vem (he comes), vêm (they come) and veem (they see): the written forms are three different words. Most differential accents were removed as well (para, pelo, pera, polo), but pôde, pôr, têm and vêm survive.

Hyphens. A prefix is a short element placed before a word to modify it, such as anti- (against), auto- (self), infra- (below), micro- (small). The hyphen appears when writing the prefix and the word together would mislead the eye or the ear, and each rule follows from a reading rule. First, a prefix ending in a vowel plus a word starting with r or s: double the consonant and drop the hyphen (antissocial, antirrugas, contrarregra). The reason is that a single s between two vowels would be read [z], and a single r between vowels is the tap, so the doubled letter preserves the [s] and the strong r. Second, a prefix ending in a vowel plus a different vowel: no hyphen (autoestima, infraestrutura, extraoficial), because two different vowels side by side cause no confusion. Third, the same vowel twice: a hyphen (micro-ondas, anti-inflamatório, contra-ataque), so that the two are not read as one. The prefixes co- and re- are exceptions and join anyway (coordenar, cooperar, reeleger). Fourth, before h: a hyphen (anti-higiênico, super-homem), because h is silent and would hide the boundary. The prefixes des- and in- are the exception and drop the h (desumano, inumano).

Some prefixes keep the hyphen always, by convention: ex- (ex-presidente), vice- (vice-diretor), pós- (pós-graduação), pré- (pré-história), recém- (recém-nascido). A prefix ending in b or r (sub-, inter-, super-, hiper-) takes a hyphen before r (sub-reitor, inter-racial) and before h (super-homem). Compound words such as guarda-chuva and segunda-feira keep their hyphen, as the first lessons noted. When in doubt about a prefix, look at the last letter of the prefix and the first letter of the word, and apply the rules in this order.

grammar.title: Punctuation in formal Portuguese
grammar.explanation:
In English a comma often marks a pause. In Portuguese a comma marks a structural boundary, and the rules are stricter. A clause is a unit with its own verb; an interpolated element is a word or phrase inserted into the middle of a sentence; an apposition is a phrase that renames the noun before it (Camila Duarte, analista de projetos). Punctuation follows the structure of these units, not the rhythm of the voice.

Never separate the subject from its verb, or a verb from its object, with a single comma: O governo investe pouco, with no comma. The only exception is an interpolated element between them, which takes a comma on both sides: O governo, segundo o relatório, investe pouco. One comma alone is an error. The same pairing applies to connectors placed in the middle of a sentence (O projeto, contudo, foi aprovado), to appositions and to the name of the person addressed.

Use a comma after an introductory adverbial element that has moved to the front: Em primeiro lugar, o acesso é desigual; Diante dos fatos, a diretoria decidiu agir. A very short adverb may go without it. In a list, Portuguese puts no comma before the final e, unlike the English serial comma: tempo, verba e apoio. Between two clauses, a comma goes before mas and before explanatory pois, but not before e when the subject is the same.

Relative clauses show why punctuation matters. A restrictive relative clause identifies which ones you mean and takes no commas: Os alunos que estudaram foram aprovados means only those who studied passed. A non-restrictive clause adds extra information and is set off by commas: Os alunos, que estudaram, foram aprovados means all of them studied, and all passed. Finally, the semicolon joins two closely related complete clauses, as in English, and stands before a connector such as contudo or por conseguinte when the connector starts the second clause: A verba acabou; por conseguinte, o projeto parou.

culture.title: A redação do ENEM e a escrita formal no Brasil
culture.text:
ENEM stands for Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio, the national exam that many Brazilian students take to enter university; ensino médio is secondary school, literally middle teaching. Its essay, a redação, is famous. The text must be a dissertativo-argumentativo essay, meaning one that sets out and defends a position, of between seven and thirty lines, on a social, scientific, cultural or political theme announced only on the day of the exam. It receives up to a thousand points, graded on five competências, or skills: command of the standard written language, understanding of the theme, organization of arguments, use of cohesive mechanisms, and a feasible intervention proposal that respects human rights. A perfect score, the nota mil, makes national headlines every year. Copying the prompt text or straying from the theme can lead to a zero.

Formal writing in Brazil is a mix of tradition and modernization. Public offices follow the Manual de Redação da Presidência da República, which recommends clear, impersonal, concise writing and limits ornate formulas such as Vossa Excelência to specific uses. The legal world still uses heavy, archaic language, known jokingly as juridiquês: jurídico plus the ending -ês, which also makes português and inglês and here means the language of the law. It has long sentences, Latin terms and formal pronouns.

In business, emails are shorter than letters but keep a formal frame: Prezado or Prezada plus the name, a clear request, Atenciosamente. Being too casual in a first message can look unprofessional, but copying the heavy style of a legal document can look old-fashioned. A good rule is to match the tone of the person you are writing to, and when in doubt, be slightly more formal. Since crase, hyphens and commas are the errors that readers notice first, the rules in this lesson are worth checking in every formal text before you send it.

questions.explanation: She says: encaminho, em anexo, meu currículo e duas cartas de recomendação.

questions.prompt: Why does the pronoun come after the verb in Coloco-me à disposição?
choices: In careful writing a verb that begins its clause takes the pronoun after it, joined by a hyphen
Because me is the subject of the sentence
Because the hyphen replaces an accent mark
Because the sentence is in the past
questions.explanation: Formal written Portuguese uses enclisis when nothing in front of the verb pulls the pronoun before it. The à is a crase: the preposition a plus the article a.

exercises.prompt: Why is antissocial written with ss?
choices: A single s between two vowels would be read as z
The prefix anti always doubles its last letter
The ss shows which syllable is stressed
It is a leftover of the old trema
exercises.explanation: A single s between two vowel sounds is [z]. Doubling it keeps the [s] sound, and because the spelling now shows the boundary clearly, the hyphen is dropped.

exercises.prompt: Why does relatório carry an accent?
choices: The accent shows that the o is nasal
It separates the word from another word spelled relatorio
The final io counts as two syllables, so the stress is third to last, which no ending predicts
Every word that ends in o needs an accent
exercises.explanation: Re-la-TÓ-ri-o is stressed on the third to last syllable. The default rule predicts no such stress, so the accent is always written. The o is open, so it is the acute.

exercises.prompt: English decision corresponds to decisão. How is the s of decisão pronounced, and why?
choices: Like s, because the tilde hardens it
Like z, because a single s between two vowel sounds is z
Like sh, because the word ends in ão
It is silent, because it is followed by ã
exercises.explanation: A single s between vowel sounds is [z]. To write the sound [s] between vowels Portuguese uses ss or ç (discussão, redação).

exercises.prompt_target: O prazo terminou; ___, o projeto foi suspenso.
exercises.hint_source: The deadline ended; consequently, the project was suspended.
exercises.explanation: The second clause is the result of the first, so any connector of consequence fits. Por conseguinte is the most formal.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence requires the grave accent (crase)?
choices: Vou a pé até o banco.
exercises.explanation: Reunião is feminine and takes the article a, and ir requires the preposition a, so the two fuse. The test: Vou ao evento gives ao, so the feminine version is à. A pé has no article, ela takes none, and volto de Curitiba shows that Curitiba takes none.

exercises.hint_source: I am referring to yesterday's meeting.
exercises.explanation: Referir-se a requires the preposition a, and reunião takes the article a; the two fuse into à.

exercises.hint_source: We will arrive at ten o'clock, as agreed.
exercises.explanation: The hour is counted with the feminine plural article as (as dez horas), and the preposition a fuses with it: às.

exercises.hint_source: We arrived in Curitiba at noon.
exercises.explanation: Formal writing uses chegar a, and Curitiba takes no article (volto de Curitiba, not da Curitiba), so there is nothing to fuse with and no accent. Speech often says chegar em, which is also accepted here.

exercises.hint_source: I am referring to that case.
exercises.explanation: The preposition a fuses with the initial a of aquele, and the fusion is written à.

exercises.prompt: Why does embora take the subjunctive while visto que takes the indicative?
choices: Visto que is always followed by a past tense
Visto que presents the reason as an established fact, while embora concedes a point without resting the argument on it
exercises.explanation: The indicative asserts something as fact. Concession and purpose present a clause that is granted or aimed at, not asserted, and take the subjunctive.

exercises.prompt_target: Embora ___ avanços, os desafios continuam grandes.
exercises.hint_source: Although there is progress, the challenges remain great.
exercises.explanation: Embora requires the present subjunctive. Haver gives haja, and existir gives existam with a plural subject.

exercises.prompt: Which is the best written-register version of porque o preço aumentou?
exercises.explanation: Nominalization turns aumentar into the masculine noun o aumento, and devido a plus o gives devido ao. An -ndo form cannot stand in for the cause clause.

exercises.prompt_target: Devido ___ chuva, o evento foi adiado.
exercises.hint_source: Due to the rain, the event was postponed.
exercises.explanation: Devido a requires the preposition a, and chuva is feminine with the article a, so the two fuse into à.
The ending -ção makes the noun feminine, so the article is a.
The suffix fixes the gender: -mento is masculine, while -ção, -dade and -ância are feminine.

exercises.prompt: Which rewrite moves Me manda o relatório into formal register?
choices: Manda o relatório pra mim, valeu.
Solicito que me envie o relatório.
Me manda o relatório, por favor.
exercises.explanation: A verb of request plus que plus the present subjunctive softens the demand. The pronoun me stands before the verb because que pulls it there. The other choices keep spoken forms or a bare command.

exercises.prompt_target: Solicito que me ___ a data da entrevista.
exercises.hint_source: I ask that you inform me of the date of the interview.
exercises.explanation: After a verb of request, the subjunctive is required. Informar belongs to the -ar group, so its subjunctive ends in e: informe.
Prezado is an adjective, so it agrees in gender with the person addressed: feminine prezada. Ilustríssima is a very formal alternative and cara a less formal one.

exercises.prompt: What does -mente attach to in atenciosamente?
choices: the feminine form of the adjective, atenciosa
the masculine form of the adjective, atencioso
exercises.explanation: Adverbs in -mente are built on the feminine form of the adjective: atenciosa plus -mente. The main stress falls on men.

exercises.hint_source: My self-esteem improved a lot this year.
exercises.explanation: A prefix ending in a vowel plus a word starting with a different vowel is written together without a hyphen: auto + estima.
Before h a hyphen is written, because the silent h would otherwise hide the boundary between prefix and word.

exercises.prompt_target: Os jovens não ___ muito hoje em dia.
exercises.hint_source: Young people do not read much these days.
exercises.explanation: The eles form of lê is leem. Since 2009 the circumflex is dropped from a doubled e, but the two forms are still different words: lê, leem.
A comma must not separate the subject from the verb, or the verb from its complement, unless an inserted element sits between them, with a comma on each side.

exercises.prompt_target: Ele estudou muito; ___, não passou no concurso.
exercises.hint_source: He studied a lot; however, he did not pass the exam.
exercises.explanation: Any connector of contrast that can open the second clause fits. Mas does not, because it cannot follow a semicolon or be followed by a comma.

exercises.prompt_source: I am writing to express my interest in the position.
answers: Venho por meio desta manifestar meu interesse pela vaga.
Escrevo para manifestar meu interesse pela vaga.
Escrevo para expressar meu interesse pela vaga.
Venho por meio desta manifestar o meu interesse pela vaga.
Escrevo para manifestar meu interesse na vaga.
Estou escrevendo para manifestar meu interesse pela vaga.
Estou escrevendo para expressar meu interesse pela vaga.
Venho por meio desta expressar meu interesse pela vaga.
Escrevo para manifestar o meu interesse pela vaga.
Envio, em anexo, o meu currículo.
Encaminho, em anexo, o meu currículo.
Estou enviando, em anexo, meu currículo.
Segue, em anexo, o meu currículo.

exercises.explanation: With coloco-me the pronoun follows the verb that opens the clause, and à is the crase of a plus a; before sua the crase is optional.

exercises.prompt_source: Because of the increase in prices, families bought less.
answers: Devido ao aumento dos preços, as famílias compraram menos.
Em virtude do aumento dos preços, as famílias compraram menos.
Por causa do aumento dos preços, as famílias compraram menos.
Devido ao aumento de preços, as famílias compraram menos.
Em razão do aumento dos preços, as famílias compraram menos.
Por conta do aumento dos preços, as famílias compraram menos.
Em virtude do aumento de preços, as famílias compraram menos.
exercises.explanation: Nominalize aumentar into o aumento and join it with a preposition of cause.
